CANNA   ANGUSTIFOLIA.

C.    ANG.        CANNA    GLAUCA.       PORTUG.  :      IMBIRI.


THIS  plant  inhabits  damp  regions,  or  the  borders  of  brooks.
Its  stem  is  erect,  cylindrical,  growing  to  a  height  of  about
six  feet  out  of  a  rhizoma  sending  off  numerous  rootlets.  It  is
provided  with  knots,  whence  arise  large  alternate  clasping
leaves,  whose  lanceolate  limbs  have  strong  midribs,  sending
off  fine  parallel  transverse  nerves.  At  its  summit  the  stem
bears  the  flower-bearing  pedicels.  Flowers  alternate,  on
short  peduncles,  and  accompanied  by  bracts.  The  corol  has
